g_policy.reason: The card is opt-in and the offer copy states the reward (3 Advanced reasoning answers today). Declining ('Not now') leaves home unchanged, and the 'if the ad fails' field covers both no-fill and unverified play.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward is 3 Advanced reasoning mode answers until midnight, which has no cash value and cannot be withdrawn or transferred.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger is a first app open after 3 or more days without a session by a non-subscriber. That is an app event and needs no chat content.

g_no_free_removal.reason: The proposal removes nothing free ('removes nothing free: yes'). It only adds a temporary sample of a paid feature.

g_brand_safety.reason: The offer is a dismissible card in the s01 home chrome, and s01 is rated safe. It is not inside a conversation or over a chat screen.

c1_revealed_value.reason: Advanced reasoning mode is a paid Luzia+ feature (paywall bullet l02 / s02.e03), so the app charges for the resource the reward gives.

c2_evidence.reason: The offer copy says 'All your past chats will be lost in 30 days if you do not upgrade to Luzia+'. That is a claim about current app behavior, and no mechanic or element in the product model supports it.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: The sample ends after 3 answers or at midnight and is capped at once per gap. The full feature stays behind the paid plans.

c5_moment.reason: The card appears on the home screen when the user returns and interrupts no task in progress. It is dismissible and sits on a persistent surface.

c6_fits_simula.reason: The unit is a play-to-earn sponsored game. The reward is granted after a verified play ('If the play isn't confirmed... try again'), and the trigger is a detectable app-open event.

c7_specific.reason: The idea names this app's Advanced reasoning mode (s02.e03), the Luzia+ badge (s01.e02), the Chats home card placement, and the 3-day trial button.

other_concern: The copy uses a fabricated data-loss threat to pressure users into subscribing, which is deceptive and risks store-policy and trust problems. The cost claim (real model time per answer) and the market-tier adjustments are unsupported predictions, but they are not counted as failures.
